🎙
Welcome address by Russian Ambassador to South Africa and Lesotho Roman Ambarov on the occasion of the
opening of new Sputnik Africa bureaus in South Africa and Tanzania
(20 October 2026)
Distinguished colleagues,
Ladies and gentlemen,
It is a real pleasure to join you today for the opening of the new
Sputnik Africa
bureaus here in Johannesburg and Tanzania.
For me, this is more than the opening of new offices. It reflects our shared commitment to
strengthening information ties and creating more opportunities for Russians and Africans
to learn more about each other.
Today,
Russian news outlets reach audiences in more than 40 African countries and broadcast in six languages.
This reflects the importance Russia attaches to direct communication with African audiences.
We live in a time when
information is increasingly politicised,
and it is not always easy to distinguish facts from disinformation
. That is why professional journalism, access to diverse sources and the opportunity to hear different perspectives are more important than ever.
Rossiya Segodnya group has established a significant presence across the African continent.
As a member of the African Union of Broadcasting and a recipient of several journalism awards, it has earned recognition in the international professional community.
🇷🇺
🇿🇦
I am particularly pleased that Johannesburg is becoming home to a new Sputnik editorial centre.
South Africa is of great importance to Russia, it is our strategic partner
. I am confident that this bureau will contribute to a richer and more diverse picture of our country in the local media landscape.
I hope that
South Africans will discover more about the real Russia
– its people, rich cultural heritage, traditions and contemporary achievements. Equally, I believe that
Russian audiences will gain a deeper appreciation of Africa
– its remarkable diversity, history, colourful and vibrant culture, and the many opportunities this country has to offer.
Ultimately, good journalism is about more than delivering news. It helps people see beyond stereotypes, understand different perspectives and recognise what they have in common.
☝️
This is also why media cooperation will be among the key themes of the upcoming
Russia-Africa Media Forum,
which will take place in Moscow on 28-29 October alongside the
Third Russia-Africa Summit.
I congratulate the entire Rossiya Segodnya and Sputnik Africa team on this important milestone. I wish you every success in your work, compelling stories, professional achievements and, above all, the trust of your audiences.
May these new bureaus become much more than editorial offices.
May they become bridges of dialogue, mutual understanding and friendship between Russia and Africa, and between the people of our countries.
Thank you.
#RussiaAfrica
#RussiaSouthAfrica
#AmbassadorAmbarov

item.description: ☢️ Zaporozhskaya Nuclear Power Plant ( #ZNPP ): ⚡️ On the evening of October 20, a Ukrainian UAV attacked a bus belonging to the NPP . The bus had already dropped off employees in the city and was returning without passengers. The vehicle was damaged in the attack. No one was injured. Behind this report lies a constant threat to the people who ensure ZNPP safety every day . They face danger at work and on their journeys to and from the plant. ▪️ Since the attacks escalated in April this year, 10 nuclear industry workers have been killed and around 40 injured . Each number represents a life cut short or changed forever, leaving families, loved ones and colleagues facing irreparable loss and suffering. The ZNPP staff continue to carry out their duties under a constant threat to their lives . *** ⚡️ On October 21, a Ukrainian drone once again attacked a bus used to transport ZNPP personnel. Having dropped off employees after the day shift, the bus was returning to the garage. ▪️ The driver was killed in the attack. The second attack on the plant’s transport in two consecutive days proves that these strikes are deliberate . They pose a direct threat to the people who ensure ZNPP operation and safety. Personnel must not become targets, whether at work or on their journeys to and from the plant. Attacks on the people who ensure the safety of the Zaporozhskaya NPP are unacceptable . #KievRegimeCrimes

🇷🇺
🇰🇿
Thirty-four years ago – on
October 22, 1992
– diplomatic relations were established between
the Russian Federation
and
the Republic of Kazakhstan.
The peoples of our countries are bound together by closely aligned cultural, spiritual and moral values, a centuries-old history of coexistence within a single state, and shared achievements and victories.
Russian-Kazakhstani relations are grounded in strong historical ties of friendship, mutual trust and respect for each other’s interests, and are underpinned by a
strategic partnership and alliance.
🤝
The leaders of our countries, who have developed close and cordial personal ties over years of collaboration,
hold regular meetings and telephone conversations
to exchange views on both current bilateral matters and issues on the regional and global agendas.
At the end of May this year, President of the Russian Federation
Vladimir Putin
paid a state visit to Kazakhstan.
Following talks with President of the Republic of Kazakhstan
Kassym-Jomart Tokayev
, a number of bilateral documents were signed, including
the Joint Statement on the Seven Foundations of Friendship and Neighbourliness between the Peoples of Russia and Kazakhstan.
In October 2025, Foreign Minister of the Russian Federation
Sergey Lavrov
held talks
with Foreign Minister of the Republic of Kazakhstan
Yermek Kosherbayev
during his first official foreign visit to Moscow. On April 30, 2026, Sergey Lavrov, in turn,
paid an official visit to Kazakhstan.
On 25 September, on the sidelines of the High-Level Week of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly,
Sergey Lavrov
met
with Minister of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan
Mukhtar Tileuberdi.
📈
Russia is one of Kazakhstan’s leading trade and economic partners.
At the end of 2025, bilateral trade volume
totalled $27.4 billion.
Our country also remains the largest investor in the Kazakhstani economy.
Russian capital is present in numerous sectors, including metallurgy, mechanical engineering, energy, and pharmaceuticals.
Russia and Kazakhstan play an important role in advancing integration processes in the post-Soviet space. Our countries were among
the founders of the Eurasian Economic Union
(
#EAEU
) and today cooperate actively within the
#CIS
, the
#CSTO
and the
#SCO
.
💬
From
Sergey Lavrov
’s
opening remarks
during talks with Foreign Minister of the Republic of Kazakhstan
Yermek Kosherbayev
(Astana, April 30, 2026)
:
Kazakhstan and Russia are
close neighbours and allies.
Our people are bound by centuries-long traditions of friendship and mutual respect. These relations are enshrined in numerous interstate documents.
One of the most important aspects of the quality of our relations is our shared memory of Victory in the Great Patriotic War. We always celebrate the anniversaries of the Great Victory together and hold special events in both Kazakhstan and the Russian Federation.
🎉
We offer our warmest congratulations to our Kazakh colleagues and friends on our shared holiday. We reaffirm our confidence in the further dynamic and steady development of friendly relations and the expansion of Russian-Kazakhstani allied ties.
#RussiaKazakhstan

🎙
Excerpt from Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s
remarks
at a meeting with university graduates entering the Russian diplomatic service
(Moscow, October 20, 2026)
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
One of the lessons bequeathed to us by the founding fathers of the UN is
to prevent the revival of the Nazism they defeated.
It seemed that this task had long been accomplished and everyone had repented… But no!
The metastases are spreading very quickly.
To a large extent, this was used as
a political instrument by bringing a Nazi regime to power in Ukraine
.
Ursula von der Leyen
and others now say they
“must stand with Ukraine as long as it takes”
because it
“defends European values”
.
This means that “European values” include a blanket ban on the Russian language in education, the media, culture and even everyday life
. A legislative ban on an entire language –
an official language of the UN
. In fact, practically everyone there still speaks it, even those imposing the ban.
☝️
This hypocrisy shows only that these bans are intended
not to eradicate the Russian language
(no one could seriously expect to achieve that),
but to undermine Russia’s interests as much as possible and divide the Russian World.
There is
no other country
where an entire language is banned.
On October 19,
at a press conference in Tehran
, I was asked to what extent the Ukraine conflict involves ideological and religious motives. I replied that
banning a language is unprecedented
, and that
the West’s silence
– indeed, it is not even keeping silent, but calling Ukrainians
“defenders of European values”
–
is very telling
.
👉
In Iran
, where I spoke at
a joint press conference
with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi,
Hebrew is not banned:
the Jewish community is thriving and synagogues are open.
In Israel, neither Arabic nor Farsi is banned
. There are many such examples.
So the West’s indulgence of and cover for this policy pursued by Kiev is very telling.
This is to say nothing of
the de facto ban on the Ukrainian Orthodox Church
, the creation some ten years ago of a quasi-church structure called the
“Orthodox Church of Ukraine”
, and attempts to forcibly close churches belonging to the canonical Church.
They have not succeeded in everything, but the West encourages this.
Nor have I mentioned the torchlight marches
, including those in present-day Kiev, Lvov and other cities (which you have surely seen), Nazi symbols, or the reburial of the remains of criminals –
Banderite executioners
– on the sacred grounds of the Kiev Pechersk Lavra. They announce the opening of a
“pantheon of heroes”
.
❗️
Zelensky kneels before the remains of this filth, and the West applauds.
I see no sign that the West disapproves.
On the contrary, militarist sentiments are resurging in Germany, Italy and Japan.
Finland
, which was our neighbour (and, we thought, a friend),
changed immediately as soon as the pendulum swung the other way
. All those underlying instincts resurfaced – the same ones that once made the Finns, like most other European countries, Hitler’s accomplices and participants in
the siege of Leningrad
, and so on.
This task will therefore remain a priority for our foreign policy.
🕯
2026 marked
the first observance
of
the Day of Remembrance for the Victims of the Genocide of the Soviet People
, established by
Federal Law No. 523-FZ of December 29, 2025
. We will work to ensure that this issue is not merely raised at international forums, but
receives the broadest possible international recognition.
The Russian MFA
will take this new factor into account in its work to prevent the revival of Nazi ideology.

📃
Letter to the Editor,
The Hill Times Newspaper
,
by Counsellor Igor Prokopiev
(
October 21, 2026
)
following a panel discussion hosted by the Canadian Network to Abolish Nuclear Weapons and the Canadian Pugwash Group on October 1
,
2026
✍️
I had the pleasure of participating in
the Oct. 1 panel on nuclear disarmament
hosted by the
Canadian Network to Abolish Nuclear Weapons
and the
Canadian Pugwash Group
, and would like to highlight Russia’s position that was presented during that discussion as well.
Nuclear disarmament is a noble cause
and a goal the international community shall pursue in the long run. Unfortunately,
it cannot be treated as a separate issue in a vacuum
. Thus, it can be achieved only in a broader context of general and complete disarmament as enshrined in the Non-Proliferation Treaty of which we’re all members and to which we all adhere.
And geopolitical context does matter.
🌐
Nuclear disarmament is a derivative of the overall state of international security
. So, before proceeding to disarming,
trust between various sides has to be rebuilt
. Preferably, on the basis of a truly collective, universal, and indivisible security system where security of some cannot be achieved at the expense of the security of others.
☝️
Until then, Russia reserves its
sovereign right to keep at its disposal strategic arms as strictly defensive means that can only be used as a response
. The very limited number of cases is described in
Russia’s Fundamentals of State Policy on Nuclear Deterrence
.
[...]
We wish the bilateral
New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (START) with the United States
could last longer
, but it has expired.
As a sign of a goodwill and responsibility, my government decided to voluntarily observe the treaty limits
- given that is done by both parties. Russia seeks neither numerical parity with others nor wishes to engage in a new nuclear arms race. For now, it exercises the principle of reasonable self-sufficiency.
START was a great tool purpose built for its time.
But talks on further nuclear reductions require more than Russia and the U.S. First and foremost, it needs the United Kingdom and France as members of NATO that present itself as a nuclear alliance
. Without them on board, we cannot have true transparency and predictability of intent.

Comment
by Aide to the President of Russia Yury Ushakov following Vladimir Putin’s meeting with Special Envoy of the US President Steven Witkoff
(October 21, 2026)
💬
Yury Ushakov
: As always,
today’s discussion
was
substantive and frank
, lasting almost three hours.
Following up on
Vladimir Putin’s
telephone conversation
with
Donald Trump
on October 9, the exchange of views continued on
ways to achieve a lasting and sustainable peace
.
Russia's President
praised the mediation efforts
of the US Administration, Donald Trump personally and his special envoys to find mutually acceptable solutions.
☝️
It is important to note that the possible resumption of trilateral talks involving representatives of Russia, the US and Ukraine was discussed in specific terms
.
As you know,
the Ukrainian regime itself thwarted their planned resumption
immediately after
the State Duma
elections by launching massive strikes on the main voting day against Moscow, other cities, polling stations and election commission staff directly, some of whom were killed.
The situation was reviewed again,
taking into account, among other things, the signals received from the Americans.
Our President informed Steve Witkoff that
we are
, in principle,
ready to resume these trilateral talks between November 10 and 19
, focusing on
👉
the central issue: building a security framework for Russia and Ukraine after the conflict ends
. The American representative said that President Trump would undoubtedly welcome this decision with great satisfaction.
Vladimir Putin asked Steve Witkoff to convey
his gratitude to US First Lady Melania Trump
for her
humanitarian efforts
, particularly in
reuniting children with their families
, as well as for her mediation in resolving
the grave humanitarian situation in the Russian town of Alyoshki
in the Kherson Region.
***
There was also an exchange of views on
the situation in the Middle East
, primarily, of course,
developments surrounding Iran
. Russia reaffirmed its readiness to continue helping to find
political and diplomatic ways
to resolve the Iranian issue.
🇷🇺
🇨🇳
🇺🇸
Naturally, today’s discussion also touched on a matter attracting considerable attention worldwide:
the possible first-ever meeting of the leaders of Russia, China and the US
during
the APEC Summit in Shenzhen
, China, this November.
None of the three capitals
– Moscow, Washington or Beijing –
has rejected this idea
.
Our Chinese friends
,
as hosts of the APEC Summit
,
are already undertaking preparations for it
. If circumstances are favourable, they will, of course, include this meeting in the programme of events in Shenzhen.
We put forward
several practical suggestions
regarding the substance of the possible trilateral talks.

We have already met three times this year ( 1 , 2 , 3 ) , and, as agreed, we will have an opportunity to meet again at the APEC Summit in Shenzhen this November. The Russia-China Summit talks produced new key agreements on developing bilateral relations of comprehensive partnership and strategic cooperation . The main efforts to implement them are, of course, being undertaken by our two Governments. We are grateful for your personal contribution to developing Russian-Chinese ties and for the constructive approach that your colleagues in the Government of China take to all these matters. ☝️ Overall, I would like to note that relations between Russia and China are developing very successfully and dynamically . . The main efforts to implement them are, of course, being undertaken by our two Governments. The government is precisely the body responsible for putting all our main areas of cooperation into practice.
Today, you and Prime Minister of Russia Mikhail Mishustin held
the 31st regular meeting of the Russian and Chinese heads of government
. Over its 30 years, this mechanism has proved effective and valuable.
We are grateful for your personal contribution
to developing Russian-Chinese ties and for the constructive approach that your colleagues in the Government of China take to all these matters.
☝️
Overall, I would like to note that relations between Russia and China are developing very successfully and dynamically
. They are based on the principles of equality, mutual respect, mutual benefit and consideration for each other’s interests. Our relations do not depend on the international situation and are not directed against anyone.
Trade and economic ties are growing
, and we will continue to expand practical cooperation in all key areas. We are working together in energy, information technology, space and the peaceful use of nuclear energy.
I would like to highlight the substantial progress in agricultural trade
: turnover
increased by 34%
in the first eight months of 2026.
Cooperation in the humanitarian sphere is also growing stronger
. Events under
the cross Years of Education
, which President Xi Jinping and I
officially launched
in Beijing in May, are proceeding successfully.
I know that a major event in China’s domestic political life –
the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China
– will take place next week, on October 26-29.
🤝
I wish our Chinese friends
every success
in holding this important event.

item.title: ⚡️ On October 21, Latvian Chargé d’Affaires a.i. Ramona Krasovska was summoned to the Russian Foreign Ministry.
item.description: ⚡️ On October 21, Latvian Chargé d’Affaires a.i. Ramona Krasovska was summoned to the Russian Foreign Ministry. A strong protest was expressed over the Latvian MFA demand to dismiss all staff of the social welfare office within the Consular Section of the Russian Embassy in Riga . This jeopardises pension payments and social support for nearly 6,000 Russian military pensioners and their family members residing in Latvia. It was stressed that these actions by the Latvian authorities violate the country’s obligations under the 1994 Russian-Latvian intergovernmental agreement on social protection for Russian military pensioners and their families . Russia has always fulfilled its obligations to Russian military pensioners and their family members living in Latvia, rigorously and in full. ❗️ The Latvian authorities bear full responsibility for this artificially created crisis in military pension payments. The Latvian side was strongly urged to strictly observe the letter and spirit of the intergovernmental agreement . A corresponding note from the Russian Foreign Ministry was delivered.

President of Russia Vladimir Putin
held a meeting
with Special Envoy of the US President Steven Witkoff
(St Petersburg, October 21, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
We are very pleased to see you –
this time
in St Petersburg.
We know that you had a meeting in Norway yesterday, and
I would
, of course,
be interested to hear about its outcomes
.
I would like to thank you and President Trump for
your attention to resolving the crisis in Ukraine
.
I know that President Trump pays
particular attention
to this issue, primarily on humanitarian grounds. In our conversations, including
our most recent telephone conversation
,
he has stressed the need to end this conflict
, above all in view of the casualties among military personnel on both sides.
But, of course, this is not only about military casualties, it is also about the suffering of civilians
. In this regard, I would ask you to convey my
most sincere gratitude
not only to the President but also to his wife, First Lady
Melania Trump
, for her contribution to addressing
humanitarian issues
.
🤝
I also believe both Sides would be interested in discussing
our plans to restore bilateral relations and Russian-American contacts
, including economic cooperation.
If you would be willing to share them, I would also be very interested to hear
your assessments of the situation in the Middle East and around Iran
. You know that we have
a special relationship of trust with Iran, with our Iranian partners and friends,
built over decades.
❗️
If we can do anything at all to help resolve
this crisis
, we will gladly do so.
You are also well aware of our proposals in this regard.
These and other topics could certainly be central to our discussions today, including
a possible meeting in China
. I have some thoughts on this that I would like to share with you as well.
Please convey my most sincere thanks to President Trump for
his efforts to resolve the crisis in Ukraine
.
***
💬
Vladimir Putin:
As for diesel, once both Sides
announced
that supplies would be delivered to the US,
global diesel prices immediately fell by 5-6
%.
We are preparing shipments right now, with several tankers being readied at once
.
The first tanker
, carrying 40,000 tonnes,
will depart in two or three days
, and the others will follow one after another. The key is to ensure that the financial arrangements are in place so that everything works.
☝️
As for farmers
– I know President Trump has even mentioned this in our telephone conversations –
we could also supply fertilisers to the US market, and in substantial quantities
.
